subject: Helios — slope autoscale guardrails & SLA exception
messages:
From: Yasmin Lee <yasmin@helios.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Helios Ops <ops@helios.ai>, Helios Procurement <procurement@helios.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity bump request: May–Jul surge & SLA coverage

Hi Chloe,

We’re looking at a sustained increase in inference traffic for our recommendation service that starts mid-May and runs through July. Q1 usage attached (helios_q1_usage_summary.csv) — you’ll see a recurring daily tail that’s been growing ~18% month-over-month.

Short ask: can Redwood provision additional Dedicated GPUs for May–July (targeting A100-equivalent capacity) and confirm whether we can get an SLA carve-out if the burst pushes our p50 latency above 350ms during the surge window? Procurement also wants a simple pricing line and an ETA for capacity live.

High-level target: ~8 additional GPUs steady, with ability to burst +4 for short spikes. We prefer a temporary/commit ramp rather than a long-term re-commit.

Thanks — can we do a quick call today or tomorrow?

— Yasmin
Yasmin Lee
Head of ML Platforms, Helios.ai
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>
To: Yasmin Lee <yasmin@helios.ai>
Cc: Helios Ops <ops@helios.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity bump request: May–Jul surge & SLA coverage

Hi Yasmin — thanks for the summary and the Q1 file. I skimmed the CSV and see the same tail you mentioned. Two quick items:

1) We can offer a short-term dedicated pool with a slope/gradual-commit approach (lower initial commit, automated step-ups tied to observed 7-day utilization thresholds). That reduces your near-term commitment while giving predictable capacity as traffic grows.

2) SLA exception: we can provision an elevated latency SLO window for the surge period if we agree guardrails (burst pool size, rollback thresholds, and routing priorities). I’ll include the draft SLA-exception form and a pricing sketch.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal sizing + pricing (we’ll share a short calc) — target EOD tomorrow.
- 30-min sync to agree thresholds and the mutual action plan (can you do 14:00 PT tomorrow?)
- Procurement: if the revised quote is signed by May 20, we can apply a one-time usage credit (details to follow).

Attaching: redwood_slope_pricing_sheet.xlsx and sla-exception-form.pdf (drafts).

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.inference | +1 415 555 0124

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity bump request: May–Jul surge & SLA coverage — sizing proposal

Hi team — I took a pass on sizing after looking at the Q1 tail and the growth rate. High-level recommendation:

- Baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for May 12 – Jul 31 (consistent with Helios ask).
- Burst pool: 4 GPUs (shared, pre-warmed) for short spikes up to 15 minutes; automated pop-in when 95th percentile queue depth crosses threshold.
- Autoscale slope: start at 50% of target reserve for the first week, then step to 75% after 7 days if 7-day avg utilization > 70%, then to 100% if > 80%.

Expected economics (rough):
- Incremental monthly burn (baseline): ~$64k/month for the 8 GPUs (list price used for estimate), burst pool add-on ~$12k/month counted only when active.
- If procurement signs by 2026-05-20 we can apply a 10% one-time usage credit for the first billing cycle (applies to baseline committed units).

Operational notes:
- We’ll instrument per-route token-level cost and latency dashboards; Redwood Console will emit an alert and automatic rollback if p50 latency > 350ms for a sustained 15-minute window during the surge (this is the SLA-exception guardrail).
- We recommend a short warm-up period (48 hours) after initial allocation to populate KV caches and avoid cold-inference spikes.

I’ve attached the quick calc (redwood_slope_pricing_sheet.xlsx) — it has line items and a one-page sample invoice.

If this looks okay I’ll draft the contract amendment and loop in legal for a temporary SLA carve-out.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Dedicated Capacity | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Subject: Re: RE: Capacity bump request: May–Jul surge & SLA coverage — sizing proposal

Thanks Ben — the slope approach makes sense. A few clarifying items from our side:

- For the SLA carve-out: we need written confirmation that Redwood will not trigger customer-impacting throttles during the agreed surge window unless the rollback thresholds are met. Can you specify exact thresholds and the escalation path?
- Monitoring: can Redwood expose per-shard latency traces in Console so our SREs can validate the warm-up?
- Procurement timeline: we can get PO ready within 10 business days but may not sign before May 20. Is the 10% credit firm only if signed by May 20?

Attaching: internal procurement timeline (for reference).

— Yasmin
Yasmin Lee
Head of ML Platforms, Helios.ai

Date: 2026-05-06T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: RE: Capacity bump request & SLA exception — next steps

Yasmin — appreciate the quick turnaround and the procurement visibility. Short answers and next steps below.

SLA carve-out specifics (draft):
- Redwood will not throttle Helios traffic for inferred model endpoints during the agreed surge window (May 12–Jul 31) unless one of the following is true:
  a) p50 latency > 350ms sustained for 15 minutes AND p95 latency > 800ms, or
  b) sustained CPU/GPU thermal fault or hardware failure requiring capacity isolation.
- Escalation path: automatic PagerDuty alert to Helios SRE group + Redwood CS lead; CS lead has authority to approve immediate rollback.
- Console exports: we’ll enable per-shard latency traces and token-level cost breakdown for the reserved pool.

Commercials:
- Baseline reserve: 8 GPUs (May 12–Jul 31) + 4-GPU burst pool.
- If PO is signed by 2026-05-20 we’ll honor the 10% first-cycle usage credit; otherwise standard pricing applies. We can include a 30-day re-eval clause if utilization materially changes.

Mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Redwood: finalize amendment & SLA-exception draft (Ben + Legal) — target 2026-05-07 EOD.
2) Helios: confirm PO ETA and decision owner — Yasmin to share by 2026-05-10.
3) Ops prep: Redwood will schedule pre-warm (48h) and observability onboarding on sign + 24h prior to live.
4) Production go-live: target May 12, contingent on PO + signed amendment + pre-warm complete.

Next immediate items:
- I’ll send the amendment + DocuSign link after Ben and Legal sign-off. (DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/echo/abcdef123456)
- Ben: please confirm the final pricing line once legal is looped.

Thanks — we’ll stay on the sync path.

Best,
